_about: A small demo library for tests (tests/demo_data.py) and for trying the app (scripts/seed_demo.py).
Papers are well-known public works with their real titles, years, venues and identifiers. Long author lists are
shortened to the first authors and the last author. Abstracts, summaries, notes, claims, concepts and the
conversation are short paraphrases written for this file. Users are fictional (demo_*).
Deliberate quirks: 'ddpm_stub' is a citation stub of the DDPM paper under its 10.48550 DOI (a duplicate the merge
scan must find); 'unet' is a reference that is only cited, never added; 'reading_group' is a private project.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.abstract: Introduces the Transformer, a sequence transduction architecture built only from attention layers, without recurrence or convolution, which trains faster and set new results in machine translation.
papers.summary: Self-attention replaces recurrence; multi-head attention and positional encodings make the model parallel and strong on translation.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.abstract: Shows that diffusion probabilistic models, trained with a weighted variational bound linked to denoising score matching, generate high-quality images.
papers.summary: A fixed forward process adds Gaussian noise step by step; a network learns to predict that noise and so to reverse the chain.

papers.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Unifies score-based models and diffusion models as stochastic differential equations whose reverse-time process depends on the score of the perturbed data distribution.
papers.summary: Continuous-time view of diffusion: forward SDE, reverse SDE and a probability-flow ODE, all driven by a learned score function.

papers.title: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract: Separates the design choices of diffusion models (noise schedule, preconditioning, sampler, training loss) and tunes each one, improving sample quality with fewer network evaluations.
papers.summary: A modular framework for diffusion design choices with a second-order Heun sampler and network preconditioning.

papers.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
papers.abstract: Trains continuous normalizing flows without simulation by regressing vector fields of fixed conditional probability paths, including diffusion paths and optimal-transport paths.
papers.summary: Simulation-free training of continuous flows; optimal-transport paths give straighter trajectories than diffusion paths.

papers.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
papers.abstract: Presents AlphaFold, a neural network that predicts protein structures from sequence with atomic accuracy in many cases, using evolutionary, physical and geometric constraints.
papers.summary: Evoformer blocks over MSA and pair representations feed a structure module that outputs atom coordinates directly.

papers.title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
papers.abstract: Extends structure prediction to complexes of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions and modified residues with a diffusion-based architecture.
papers.summary: Replaces the structure module with a diffusion module over raw atom coordinates and a simpler Pairformer trunk.

papers.title: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion
papers.abstract: Fine-tunes the RoseTTAFold structure prediction network as a denoising diffusion model for protein backbones, enabling design of binders, symmetric assemblies and enzyme scaffolds.
papers.summary: A structure predictor turned denoiser generates new backbones; designs were confirmed experimentally, including by cryo-EM.

papers.title: Evolutionary-scale prediction of atomic-level protein structure with a language model
papers.abstract: Scales protein language models to billions of parameters and shows that structural information emerges in their representations, enabling fast single-sequence structure prediction with ESMFold.
papers.summary: ESM-2 language model plus ESMFold head: structure prediction without multiple sequence alignments, fast enough for metagenomic scale.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Graph Neural Networks
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
papers.abstract: Surveys graph neural networks and groups them into recurrent, convolutional, graph autoencoder and spatial-temporal families, with applications, benchmarks and open problems.
papers.summary: A taxonomy of GNN architectures with datasets and open-source implementations.

claims.text: A model built only from attention layers, without recurrence or convolution, can reach state-of-the-art translation quality.
Sampling reverses a fixed Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to the data.
Training on a simplified objective that predicts the added noise gives the best sample quality.
Score-based models and diffusion models are discretisations of the same stochastic differential equation.
Tuning sampler, preconditioning and noise distribution separately improves image quality while needing fewer sampling steps.
Continuous normalizing flows can be trained without simulation by regressing conditional vector fields.
Predicted structures reached accuracy competitive with experiment for most targets in the CASP14 assessment.
Designed binders and symmetric assemblies were validated experimentally, including by cryo-EM.
Generated backbones still need a separate sequence design step.
Atomic-level structure information emerges in language model representations as model scale grows.

conversations.title: How does flow matching relate to diffusion?

messages.content: How does @paper:"Flow Matching for Generative Modeling" relate to DDPM?

Flow matching trains a vector field along fixed probability paths. A diffusion path is one such path, so DDPM-style training is a special case; optimal-transport paths are straighter and need fewer sampling steps.
